reason: two entries carry glosses that belong to a DIFFERENT WORD, not to the reading they teach. 強請る is filed at ねだる (to pester, to beg for) but its entire English line reads "to extort, to demand", which is the ゆする entry — a learner sees 妹は誕生日に新しいバッグを強請った beside "to extort" and reads it as the sister extorting a bag. 退ける is the transitive しりぞける but its Chinese leads with 退却, the intransitive 退く. Found by the reading-mismatch check added to the N1 triage brief after 博士/はくし survived an earlier pass.

entries.why: both English glosses belong to the ゆする reading; the Chinese was already right
退却 is the intransitive 退く, not the transitive しりぞける
